decision.state: Promising intervention evidence; EDC-specific marginal cost-effectiveness not yet estimable
decision.summary: Eviction Defense Collaborative is the lead agency in San Francisco's Tenant Right to Counsel program and reports substantial legal-service and rental-assistance volume. External experiments show that representation can improve some eviction-case outcomes, but results vary by court and service model. Public sources do not isolate EDC's causal effect, incremental delivery cost, or the outcomes of the next philanthropic gift.

financialContext.summary: The FY2024 audit reports $26.20 million in revenue, $25.96 million in expenses, and $23.51 million in program-service expenses, including $8.02 million of rental and client assistance.
financialContext.boundary: These are organization-wide and program-bucket amounts. Assistance transfers must remain separate from delivery costs, and none of these totals establishes the cost or funding room of a marginal philanthropic expansion.

evidence.population: 1,800 San Francisco Tenant Right to Counsel cases across legal-aid partners in FY2022–23; EDC was lead agency
evidence.result: The city reported that 63% of full-scope clients stayed in their homes versus 45% receiving limited-scope assistance at a mandatory settlement conference. It also reported that 92% of represented tenants avoided homelessness.
evidence.transfer: The presentation does not report assignment, adjustment, organization-level results, denominators for every outcome, follow-up duration, or program cost. The differences are descriptive program statistics—not an EDC-specific causal estimate.

evidence.population: 268 low-income tenants in New York City Housing Court, randomly offered volunteer legal counsel or usual unrepresented process
evidence.result: Final judgments were entered against 22% of represented tenants and 51% of unrepresented tenants. The experiment supports a causal effect in that older NYC setting.
evidence.transfer: Different jurisdiction, era, attorney model, eligibility, and court process. The result cannot be assigned to EDC or converted into current San Francisco outcomes without an explicit transfer model.

evidence.population: 184 Massachusetts Housing Court cases offered full representation or lawyer-for-the-day and unbundled assistance
evidence.result: Full representation used substantially more attorney time but did not improve substantive outcomes in this Housing Court context. A separate District Court evaluation was more favorable, underscoring that setting and service design matter.
evidence.transfer: This is not evidence that EDC has no effect. It is evidence against assuming that more intensive representation always produces the same outcome in every court.

model.nativeOutcome: Household retaining possession or avoiding an enforced eviction at a pre-specified follow-up point
missingInputs: A named EDC program, eligible cohort, and duplicate-free household denominator for the next gift
A pre-specified outcome definition separating retained possession, favorable move-out, dismissal, settlement, and avoided homelessness
Outcome follow-up duration and complete loss-to-follow-up reporting
A credible EDC-specific counterfactual or an explicit, sensitivity-tested transfer from external causal evidence
Full incremental delivery cost with cash assistance transfers reported separately
Public-funding, reimbursement, and displacement assumptions that identify philanthropic additionality
Downside data including unsuccessful cases, repeat filings, adverse moves, and implementation constraints
model.qalyBoundary: No QALY, WELLBY, life-saved, or life-substantially-bettered conversion is published. A housing-retention model with duration, counterfactual, and incremental cost must come first.

reservations: The city program figures combine multiple legal-aid partners and do not identify an EDC-only effect.
The 63% versus 45% comparison is not reported as randomized or adjusted and may reflect vulnerability scoring and case selection.
Avoided trial is not the same as avoided eviction, housing retention, or avoided homelessness.
EDC's current impact webpage does not display a measurement year, denominator details, follow-up duration, or independent verification.
Rental and client assistance includes transfers to households; treating the transfer value as administrative delivery cost would misstate cost-effectiveness.
The reviewed public record does not identify what a new unrestricted gift would add beyond city and other public funding.
